subject: Astronomy & Space
title: Magnetars: The Strongest Magnets
description: A fast breakdown of Magnetars: The Strongest Magnets for builders.

hook.text: A magnetar's magnetic field is a trillion times stronger than Earth's. It can warp atoms into pencil shapes.

buildup.text: Magnetars are a rare type of neutron star. Only about 30 are known in the Milky Way.

discovery.text: In 2004, a magnetar 50,000 light-years away sent a gamma-ray burst that disrupted Earth's upper atmosphere.

twist.text: If a magnetar were within 1,000 km of you, its field would dissolve the molecules in your body.

climax.text: Their fields decay after about 10,000 years. Magnetars are a brief, violent phase in a neutron star's life.

punchline.text: The strongest magnets in the universe. Brief, violent, and terrifying.

quiz.question: What makes magnetars different from ordinary neutron stars?
options: They have magnetic fields a trillion times stronger than Earth's
They spin millions of times faster than regular pulsars
They are the largest type of neutron star

details.summary: Magnetars are neutron stars with magnetic fields a quadrillion (10¹⁵) times stronger than Earth's — the strongest known magnets in the universe. Their magnetic energy drives violent starquakes and gamma-ray flares.
details.whyItMatters: Magnetars demonstrate that the universe produces extreme phenomena beyond our daily experience. Their ultra-strong fields test fundamental physics and help explain mysterious bursts of gamma rays detected from across the cosmos.
takeaways: Magnetars have magnetic fields a quadrillion times Earth's
They're the strongest known magnets in the universe
Their flares and starquakes produce intense gamma-ray bursts

faq.question: How do magnetars get such strong magnetic fields?
faq.answer: The leading theory involves a dynamo effect during the neutron star's formation. If the collapsing core is convecting rapidly (churning) during the first 10-30 seconds, fluid motions can amplify the magnetic field to magnetar strength. Not all neutron stars become magnetars.

faq.question: Are magnetars dangerous from a distance?
faq.answer: A magnetar's gamma-ray flare from within the galaxy could damage Earth's ozone layer if close enough. In 2004, a magnetar flare from 50,000 light-years away briefly affected Earth's ionosphere. Fortunately, no known magnetars are close enough to pose a threat.
